DexNav becomes available with Professor Birch's first Pokédex gift. Players returning from older saves with a Pokédex gain it automatically when they continue.

## Searching
Select DexNav from the Start menu. Nearby wild-encounter terrain and actual encounter tables must be present. When there is no valid search area, a small upper-left guide explains where DexNav works; dismiss it with A, B or START.

## Approaching a target
Searching a Pokémon does **not** fail merely because you walk, run or cycle toward it. The target times out after **45 seconds**, rather than the earlier 15-second limit. Going out of signal range, manually cancelling, leaving the map, or letting the timer expire can still end a search. Reach the target to enter the normal battle.

[[shiny|Selectable shiny rates]] also apply to eligible newly generated DexNav encounters.

articles.title: Adventure Log and played days
articles.summary: A notebook of milestones, catches, and dates actually played.
articles.content:
## Open the notebook
Choose **ADVENTURE LOG** from the Start menu. It resembles a cream-and-lavender field notebook and stores up to **32 recent entries** including story milestones, locations, and one recent captured Pokémon with its level where available.

## Controls
- **Left/Right or L/R:** flip older/newer pages.
- **SELECT:** change All, Day, and Story filters.
- **Up/Down:** browse available played days in Day mode.
- **A:** return to the newest page in the active filter.
- **B or START:** close the notebook back to the pause menu.

## DAY counter
The pause menu's DAY counter measures **distinct dates actually played**, not the number of days since the cartridge began. If you play on Monday and Thursday, the skipped intervening dates do not add days. Your accumulated play hours continue normally.

Existing saves start a new journal at Day 1; the game does not invent a complete past travel history.

## Wing Survey milestones
The log now records the Kanto survey milestones, including the opening report, The Borrowed Voice fieldwork and The Quiet Current. Read the current journal dialogue from **Oak's aide in the Vermilion Fan Club** when you need a checklist of missing survey tasks; the Adventure Log records history rather than replacing that checklist.

articles.title: Da Bug
articles.summary: The special Leafhopper Pokémon and its one-time PC gift.
articles.content:
## A special Pokémon
Da Bug is a single-stage **Bug/Grass** Leafhopper Pokémon, 0.3 m tall and 1.2 kg. Its leaf-like wings help it blend into vegetation.

## One-time gift
Each new save receives one **level 5** Da Bug in Pokémon Storage. Older saves receive one in the first available PC box slot when continued. Full boxes defer the delivery until space is available; existing Pokémon are never overwritten.

Its starting moves are **Tackle, Leer, Mean Look and Absorb**. The special gift has its own independent **1/10 shiny chance**, regardless of your [[shiny|wild shiny rate]] setting.

## Progression
Da Bug does not evolve. It learns moves including Bug Bite, Leech Seed, Mega Drain, Giga Drain, Leech Life, Synthesis, Energy Ball and Bug Buzz as it levels. It is excluded from the Random starter pool because that pool requires an available evolution.

The gift is not a new wild encounter distribution.

articles.title: Kanto postgame overview
articles.summary: Where you can travel today and where construction continues.
articles.content:
## Reaching Kanto
First become Hoenn Champion. Visit **Lilycove Harbor**, speak with the League representative for the retained **Invite Ticket**, then speak to the sailor beside the normal ferry attendant. The service connects Lilycove to **Vermilion City** in both directions.

After arriving, you can also Surf between northern Hoenn Route 124 and southern Kanto Route 19 when you meet the required ticket, Champion, Surf and badge conditions. The ferry remains available.

## Currently accessible areas
The present southeastern and central route network includes Vermilion, Lavender, Fuchsia, Saffron, Celadon, Routes 6–8 and 11–19 plus Route 10, both Rock Tunnel floors and the Power Plant. A number of native FireRed-looking gates and interiors remain sealed or only partially developed. Routes 16–18 support walking or normal Emerald bikes.

Developed Kanto locations now use their **native FireRed wild slot levels**, including walking, Surf, fishing and Rock Smash. Their species distributions and rates are preserved; wild levels are no longer raised to roughly 47–54. The stronger visiting Gym teams still use the difficulty you choose. Some optional trainers and birdwatchers are present.

## Getting oriented
From the postgame PokéNav map, press **SELECT** to change the displayed region between Hoenn and Kanto. This is map *browsing*: it does not teleport you or permit cross-region Fly.

Start [[walkthrough-kanto-arrival|Chapter 15: Kanto Arrival]] for a guided continuation from the Hoenn ending. [[kanto-gyms|Four visiting Gyms]] and three [[survey|Wing Survey stages]] are playable, with Gym Leaders Surge, Koga, Erika and Sabrina. [[walkthrough-kanto-current|The Quiet Current]] reaches the Power Plant and permits an optional level 50 Zapdos challenge. Cerulean/Route 9 access, the full eight-Gym circuit and Articuno/Moltres/Mew expeditions are not open in v0.0.40.

articles.title: Kanto visiting Gym challenges
articles.summary: Four visiting Gyms, selectable teams, one-victory rules and the separate Kanto badge collection.
articles.content:
## Four challenges are playable
**Lt. Surge, Koga, Erika and Sabrina** are currently playable. See [[walkthrough-kanto-survey|Chapter 16]] and [[walkthrough-kanto-voice|Chapter 17]] for travel, Gym and fieldwork instructions.

| Leader | Standard | Champion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lt. Surge — Vermilion | 4 Pokémon, levels 52–56 | 6 Pokémon, levels 72–76 |
| Koga — Fuchsia | 4 Pokémon, levels 56–60 | 6 Pokémon, levels 76–80 |
| Erika — Celadon | 4 Pokémon, levels 54–58 | 6 Pokémon, levels 74–78 |
| Sabrina — Saffron | 4 Pokémon, levels 58–62 | 6 Pokémon, levels 78–82 |

The entrance guide asks whether to choose Champion: Yes means Champion, No means Standard. Your party is not rescaled. You can change modes before winning; declining or losing preserves the challenge.

## One victory each
**Defeat each Leader only once per save**, regardless of mode. Winning either difficulty closes both choices for that Gym and advances the same story record. Losses permit retry or reselection.

The local Trainer Card has separate Hoenn and Kanto badge strips. Left/Right, L/R or SELECT switches collections. Unearned Kanto slots are dimmed. Kanto badges do not replace the Hoenn field-use permissions.

## Still in development
Brock, Misty, Blaine and the Viridian Leader are not playable visiting challenges in v0.0.40. A full-region map does not indicate that every Gym is open.

articles.title: Wing Survey and legendary bird storyline
articles.summary: Complete three Wing Survey stages, observe or challenge Zapdos, and follow the current story endpoint.
articles.content:
## The opening report
Meet Oak's field aide in the Vermilion Pokémon Fan Club, complete Surge and Koga in either order, and return to file the opening report. The aide tracks 0/2, 1/2 or 2/2 Gym records. Winning both is not enough for the next field scenes until you speak to the aide. Follow [[walkthrough-kanto-survey|Chapter 16]] for the full route.

## The Borrowed Voice
After the first report, complete Erika and Sabrina in either order. With Erika's victory, examine leaves with the birdwatcher on Route 16, west of Celadon before the gate. With Sabrina's victory, listen with the researcher beside Route 8's grass, east of Saffron. Each observation also requires the opening report to be filed.

Return to the Vermilion Fan Club with both Gym records and both observations. The aide names any missing tasks and files the second report once all four are present. The leaf sample remains with its watcher; no special item or legendary capture is required. See [[walkthrough-kanto-voice|Chapter 17]] for directions and the teleport-pad route through Sabrina's Gym.

The evidence distinguishes a bright bird's migration from a smaller imitator. Mew is still a theory. These scenes do not produce catchable legendary battles.

## The Quiet Current
After filing The Borrowed Voice, travel north from Lavender through Rock Tunnel to Route 10's northern Center. Surf down the eastern river to the Power Plant. Isolate the west and east unused feeds in either order, then observe Zapdos at its northwest roost.

Observation is sufficient. A level 50 battle is optional and independent of Gym difficulty. Capturing Zapdos keeps it caught; fainting or fleeing allows it to return on another visit. Return to Oak's aide to file the report. Follow [[walkthrough-kanto-current|Chapter 18]] for terminal directions, preparation and the return route.

## Current endpoint
After The Quiet Current, **Seafoam’s cold water** is the next lead. That island expedition, the remaining four visiting Gyms, and new Articuno/Moltres/Mew encounters are not open in **v0.0.40**. Explore accessible areas or take the ferry home; no further report trigger is implemented yet.

articles.title: Implemented and planned content
articles.summary: A clear line between shipped systems and future ideas.
articles.content:
## Implemented now
- Emerald's core Hoenn adventure with modern EXP Share and badge-earned HM field utilities.
- National Pokédex early, Champion Rare Candies and starter-set choices.
- Wild shiny rate control, following Pokémon, DexNav improvements and Da Bug's storage gift.
- Seasons, dynamic weather, clocks and the Adventure Log with survey milestones.
- Gender-specific hairstyles, eight hair colors, full grunt costumes, Navy/Winter coats, footwear, card colors and wardrobe Apply/Cancel.
- Instant text, 25 window-frame types and first-time obtained-item descriptions.
- Kanto ferry/Surf travel, map browsing, native FireRed wild levels, four visiting Gyms and three Wing Survey stages.
- Rock Tunnel, Route 10 and the Power Plant, including optional level 50 Zapdos after making both feeds safe. Observation alone advances the survey.

## Planned or incomplete
- Brock, Misty, Blaine and the Viridian visiting-Gym challenge; the full north/west network and Kanto League continuation.
- The next Seafoam/Articuno expedition, Moltres habitat episode and final Mew story. Mew is still a research lead, not a confirmed new encounter.
- Some Kanto interiors and routes remain sealed or unpopulated. Route 9/Cerulean access is not open just because the full-region map shows those places.

## Reporting issues
The current wiki source review is **v0.0.40**. Code/build checks and verified patches do not mean every animation and route has been manually traversed. Report reproducible issues with your game version, build and emulator; see [[support|Troubleshooting and bug reports]].

articles.title: Troubleshooting and bug reports
articles.summary: Save-safe testing and where to report an issue.
articles.content:
## Common questions
**The patcher rejects my ROM.** Confirm the original, unmodified Pokémon Emerald U.S./Europe image has SHA-1 `f3ae088181bf583e55daf962a92bb46f4f1d07b7`. A different revision, previously patched file, or wrong region will fail validation.

**My clock is not advancing in real time.** Enable RTC support in the emulator; if it is unsupported, try manual bedroom time or the gameplay fallback. See [[clock|Clocks]].

**DexNav says to find encounter terrain.** Move closer to an area with valid wild-encounter data. See [[dexnav|DexNav]].

**I cannot access a planned Kanto location.** Some roads and buildings are intentionally closed while development continues. See [[status|Current scope]].

**My hair selection did not save.** A in the hairstyle/color list only keeps the choice pending; choose APPLY on the main wardrobe screen. B inside the list restores its entry value. Fixed Team costumes and underwater suits do not show ordinary hair/coat/footwear customization. See [[wardrobe|Wardrobe controls]].

**Kanto wild Pokémon are much lower-level now.** v0.0.33 restored native FireRed slot levels. Visiting Gym difficulty remains independent; this is intentional rather than a lost postgame setting.

**The Power Plant terminals will not start the survey.** File The Borrowed Voice report with Oak's aide in the Vermilion Fan Club first. Isolate both feeds before observing Zapdos. Catching it is optional. See [[walkthrough-kanto-current|The Quiet Current]].

## Report a reproducible bug
Open a GitHub issue in the [project issue tracker](https://github.com/BabyCRTTV/pokeemerald-emerald-legends/issues) and include:
- Your Legends version and Release or Debug variant.
- Emulator name/version and operating system.
- New or existing save, and any cheats/debug actions.
- Exact steps, expected result, actual result and screenshots if useful.

Keep backups of saves before using developer options or switching builds.

articles.title: Wiki policy, credits, and legal notes
articles.summary: How this wiki is maintained and what it does not distribute.
articles.content:
## Update policy
This wiki is a manually maintained documentation snapshot. A new game release **does not automatically modify these articles**. When the project owner requests a wiki update, articles can be revised to reflect new content and correct older descriptions. The wiki's own revision is independent of the ROM version.

## Companion Android app
The official wiki Android companion displays this same live GitHub Pages wiki. The app's pages update when the website is intentionally edited and the device has internet access. It does not download, patch, emulate, or contain the game ROM. The companion needs only internet access; no login, account, files, camera, contacts, or location permission is required. A fresh connection is needed for articles that are not already cached.

## Legal
Pokémon Emerald: Legends is an unofficial, non-commercial fan project, not endorsed by Nintendo, GAME FREAK, Creatures, or The Pokémon Company. Trademarks and characters belong to their owners. The public project supplies source and verified BPS patches, **not** a commercial Pokémon Emerald ROM.

## Technical sources
The [source repository](https://github.com/BabyCRTTV/pokeemerald-emerald-legends), its [feature documentation](https://github.com/BabyCRTTV/pokeemerald-emerald-legends/tree/master/docs/features), and [release history](../changelog.html) provide implementation-level detail. This wiki is curated for players rather than mirroring every engineering document.

articles.title: Interactive Pokédex and wild encounters
articles.summary: Search routes and Pokémon sprites with level ranges and encounter percentages.
articles.content:
## Explore the route-by-route Pokédex

The **[interactive Pokédex and Wild Encounter Explorer](dex.html)** displays Hoenn and Legends Kanto encounter locations, species sprites, level ranges and per-method encounter rates in an easy-to-read mobile layout. It works in the website and the Android wiki companion.

## Search by Pokémon or location

Choose **Wild encounters** to search a route or Pokémon name. Filter by Hoenn or Kanto, then choose Land, Surf, Rock Smash, Old Rod, Good Rod or Super Rod. Tap a Pokémon’s name for its full location list; tap its sprite to hear its cry.

Choose **National Pokédex** to browse the species catalogue, search by Pokédex number or name, filter by type, and find documented wild encounter sites.

## Interpreting spawn percentage

A Pokémon's spawn percentage represents the combined relative weight of its slots **after that specific method successfully starts an encounter**. It is not the chance per step. Fishing rods each have their own tables.

## Scope and availability

Currently indexed data comes from the active Legends static encounter tables reviewed at game **v0.0.40**. The catalogue includes **132 locations**, with native FireRed levels in Kanto and new Route 10, Rock Tunnel and Power Plant tables. Gift, scripted and special dynamic encounters remain separate. The optional level 50 Zapdos is a scripted battle; see [[walkthrough-kanto-current|Chapter 18]] rather than expecting it in the Power Plant walking table. A Pokémon with no listed wild location isn't necessarily unobtainable.

[**Open the Pokédex and Route Explorer**](dex.html).

articles.title: Chapter 15: The ferry to Kanto
articles.summary: Continue after the Hoenn League, collect your invitation and settle into Vermilion before starting the Wing Survey.
articles.content:
## Collect your invitation
1. Finish the Hall of Fame and credits after defeating Wallace. Continue the same save.
2. Return to **Lilycove City** and enter **Lilycove Harbor**.
3. Speak with the **Pokémon League representative** to receive the **Invite Ticket**. If the Bag is full, make room and speak again.
4. Keep the ticket: it is also your return pass. Speak to the **Kanto sailor beside the regular ferry attendant**, and agree to sail to **Vermilion City**.

You do not need to start a new game or finish Emerald's optional Battle Frontier activities to take this ferry. If the representative does not offer an invitation, confirm that you completed the Champion ending on this save. If the sailor asks for a ticket, speak to the representative first.

Before leaving, heal your team and stock up on Poké Balls, healing items, Revives and status cures. Kanto's visiting Gyms offer an easier Standard team and a stronger Champion team; your party is never automatically rescaled. You can return to Hoenn whenever you want.

## Arrive in Vermilion
Finish the port welcome scene, then walk into **Vermilion City**. The welcoming host points you to the **Pokémon Center at the north end of town** and the **Pokémon Fan Club**. Heal and save before exploring.

**Optional — Alex's friendly match:** The fan near the dock offers a six-Pokémon battle around **levels 60–64**. You can decline and return later; beating Alex is not required for the ticket, Gyms or Wing Survey. This is a trainer battle, so you cannot catch Alex's Pokémon.

The ferry remains at the port. Speak with its sailor and agree to return to **Lilycove** when you need Hoenn facilities or want to pause the Kanto story. The same retained ticket works for future crossings.

## Meet Oak's field aide
Visit the **Pokémon Fan Club in Vermilion** and speak to **Professor Oak's field aide**. This begins the **Wing Survey**, an investigation into unusual bird sightings and copied cries following Hoenn's weather crisis.

The opening task is to earn the visiting Gym records from **Lt. Surge in Vermilion** and **Koga in Fuchsia**. They can be completed in either order. Speak to the aide whenever you need a progress reminder; the journal reports which records you still need.

The sequence below starts with nearby Surge, then travels east toward Fuchsia. Already completed one of those Gyms? Keep that record and follow the remaining instructions in [[walkthrough-kanto-survey|Chapter 16: The opening report]].

## Explore without losing your place
- **North:** Route 6 connects Vermilion and Saffron. Saffron connects west to Route 7 and Celadon, and east to Route 8 and Lavender.
- **East:** Route 11 leads toward Route 12. Follow the southern route chain through Routes 13, 14 and 15 to reach Fuchsia.
- **West of Celadon:** Routes 16, 17 and 18 form an alternative path to Fuchsia. Normal Emerald bicycles and walking are supported on this developing network.

Use the highlighted maps and route encounter lists in the next chapters as you travel. The map shows the whole region for orientation; a town symbol does not mean that every FireRed location or building is currently accessible in Legends. Do not follow a vanilla FireRed story checklist for sealed buildings.

In the game's postgame **PokéNav map**, press **SELECT** to browse Hoenn or Kanto. Switching the displayed region does not teleport you or allow cross-region Fly.

## Optional sea passage
The ferry is the simplest first trip. After meeting the Champion, ticket and Surf requirements, you can also use the northern passage on **Hoenn Route 124** to reach **southern Kanto Route 19**. The reverse passage returns to Route 124. These are scripted regional crossings, not a continuous sea with additional islands to search.

Keep the Invite Ticket, and use your established field utilities for Surf. If the passage is unavailable, use the ferry instead; the sea crossing is not required for the survey.

## Ready for the first report
Before continuing, confirm that you have arrived in Vermilion, healed, and spoken to Oak's aide. Next, earn Surge and Koga's records and return to the Fan Club to file them. The optional dock battle and sea passage can wait.

Checked against Legends v0.0.40 on 12 October 2026. Route lists use the existing manual encounter snapshot; its sixteen Kanto tables use the reviewed native FireRed levels. Story and Gym progress are recorded in your game save, not in the wiki.

articles.title: Chapter 16: Vermilion, Fuchsia and the opening report
articles.summary: Choose your visiting Gym difficulty, travel to Fuchsia and file the first Wing Survey report.
articles.content:
## Choose your Gym difficulty
Save and heal before entering each visiting Gym. Its entrance guide explains the rules and asks whether you want the **Champion challenge**: **Yes selects Champion; No selects Standard**.

| Leader | Standard team | Champion team |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lt. Surge — Vermilion | 4 Pokémon, Lv. 52–56 | 6 Pokémon, Lv. 72–76 |
| Koga — Fuchsia | 4 Pokémon, Lv. 56–60 | 6 Pokémon, Lv. 76–80 |

The guide can change your selection **before you win**. Declining the Leader's battle leaves it available; losing allows a retry or a different choice. **One victory completes that Gym for this save in both modes.** You cannot beat Standard and then return for a second Champion victory. Either mode earns the same story record and Kanto badge.

These are team-level ranges, not suggested wild Pokémon levels. Your own party keeps its existing levels. Pick the mode that fits your team, then adjust moves and held items rather than expecting the game to scale automatically.

## Lt. Surge in Vermilion
1. Enter **Vermilion's Gym**, speak with the entrance guide and select your challenge.
2. Reach **Lt. Surge** and agree to the battle when ready.
3. Defeat him, then finish the victory dialogue. His report concerns unusual electrical readings and a large bird near the Power Plant.
4. Heal before leaving town. You can ask Oak's aide to review the new record now, or continue to Koga and return with both.

Ground coverage is useful against Electric opponents, and Ground-type partners normally avoid Electric damage. Check secondary types and coverage moves; a type advantage does not make a low-level Pokémon automatically safe. Bring a backup instead of relying on a single attacker.

The Power Plant clue is a story lead. The later [[walkthrough-kanto-current|Quiet Current chapter]] reaches that site after the two previous reports are filed; Surge’s victory alone does not unlock its survey interactions.

## Routes 11 and 12
Leave Vermilion **east onto Route 11** and continue toward **Route 12**. At the north–south road, take the **southern direction toward Fuchsia** rather than heading north toward Lavender.

The route panels below show the standard catches and available methods for each stop. Optional route trainers offer battles you may decline. Heal back in Vermilion if your party is worn down before committing to the longer trip, and save after important catches.

**Optional — Lavender:** The northern end of Route 12 leads toward Lavender Town. It is useful for orientation, but the native FireRed Pokémon Tower story is not a prerequisite for this Legends report. Stay on the southbound route chain if your immediate destination is Koga.

## Routes 13 to 15
Continue from Route 12 onto **Route 13**, then follow **Route 14** and **Route 15** west into **Fuchsia City**. Use signs and the game map to check the next route number when the road bends.

These routes have different encounter tables. Search each route in LegendsDex if you are looking for a particular catch; the inline lists are grouped by route and encounter method. An encounter percentage is the share within its method, not a promise that the next step will produce that Pokémon.

Bring status cures and keep at least one healthy partner available. If you want to avoid extra wild battles while travelling, use Repels; stop using them when you want to hunt the route's listed Pokémon.

## Koga in Fuchsia
1. Heal at Fuchsia's Pokémon Center, save and prepare your battle items.
2. Enter **Fuchsia's Gym** and choose Standard or Champion with its guide.
3. Follow the Gym passages toward **Koga**. If a wall blocks an apparently clear line, work around it rather than assuming that the leader can be reached directly.
4. Defeat Koga and finish his dialogue. His record concerns strange Seafoam winds and bird sightings.

Ground and Psychic coverage can help against Poison opponents, but check their other types and possible immunities. Carry Antidotes or Full Heals and avoid letting poison exhaust the whole party between attempts. If you lose, heal and speak to the guide again if you want a different mode.

Koga's Seafoam clue does not unlock a new Articuno expedition yet. Winning his visiting challenge also does not replace your existing Hoenn field-use badge requirements.

## Return and file the opening report
Return to **Vermilion's Pokémon Fan Club** and speak with **Oak's field aide**. Retracing Routes 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 is a straightforward return path. Alternatively, use the western route network through Routes 18, 17 and 16 to Celadon, then Routes 7 and 6 via Saffron.

The journal tracks **0/2, 1/2 or 2/2 opening Gym records**. If it names a missing Leader, complete that challenge and return. Once Surge and Koga are both recorded, the aide files the **opening report** and introduces the next fieldwork. You must actually speak with the aide to file it; simply winning both battles is not enough for the next observations.

You can review the clues again when offered. They describe several habitats and an unidentified imitator; no legendary capture is required for this report.

## Check your Kanto badges
Open the local **Trainer Card** and use **Left/Right, L/R or SELECT** to switch between the Hoenn and Kanto badge strips. Surge and Koga's victories appear in the Kanto collection; unused slots remain dimmed. This display does not remove your eight Hoenn badges or change their field permissions.

With the opening report filed, continue to [[walkthrough-kanto-voice|Chapter 17: The Borrowed Voice]]. Erika and Sabrina can be challenged in either order, followed by their matching observations.

Checked against Legends v0.0.40 on 12 October 2026. Route lists use the existing manual encounter snapshot; its sixteen Kanto tables use the reviewed native FireRed levels. Story and Gym progress are recorded in your game save, not in the wiki.

articles.title: Chapter 17: Celadon, Saffron and The Borrowed Voice
articles.summary: Complete the next two visiting Gyms, examine Route 16’s leaves and investigate the copied calls on Route 8.
articles.content:
## Begin the second survey
First complete Surge and Koga's challenges and **file the opening report with Oak's aide at the Vermilion Fan Club**. The aide now lists the missing tasks for **The Borrowed Voice**.

Four tasks complete this stage: **Erika's Gym record, Sabrina's Gym record, the Route 16 leaf observation and the Route 8 call observation**. You may do Erika and Sabrina in either order. Each field scene needs the opening report plus its own Leader's victory; you do not have to finish both Gyms before starting either observation.

| Leader | Standard team | Champion team |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Erika — Celadon | 4 Pokémon, Lv. 54–58 | 6 Pokémon, Lv. 74–78 |
| Sabrina — Saffron | 4 Pokémon, Lv. 58–62 | 6 Pokémon, Lv. 78–82 |

The same one-victory rule applies. At the entrance guide, Yes selects Champion and No selects Standard. You can change modes before winning, or retry after a loss; winning either mode completes both choices for that Gym. Save and heal before each attempt.

## Route 6 to Saffron
From Vermilion, go **north along Route 6 into Saffron City**. Saffron is your central junction: its **west gate leads to Route 7 and Celadon**, and its **east gate leads to Route 8 and Lavender**.

Heal in Saffron before choosing your next stop. You can challenge Sabrina first, or follow the order below by travelling west to Erika. The town selector above provides quick access if you are returning to a particular Gym or field scene.

## Route 7 and Celadon Gym
Travel **west through Route 7 into Celadon City**. Erika's Gym is in the **south of the city**, beyond its garden approach. Use **Cut on the small tree** when it blocks your way, using Legends' field utilities and existing Hoenn badge permissions.

Speak to the entrance guide and choose your team difficulty. Continue through the garden to **Erika**, agree to her battle and finish the victory dialogue. Her clue points to a birdwatcher on **Route 16**, where leaves fell after a bright wing passed overhead.

Fire, Flying, Ice and Bug coverage can help against Grass opponents. Bring status cures for sleep or poison, and consider your partner's other type before assuming it has a safe matchup. If the team is too strong, losing does not lock you out of selecting Standard on the next attempt.

## Route 16 leaf observation
1. Leave Celadon **west onto Route 16**.
2. Speak to the **birdwatcher beside the road before the gate**.
3. Agree to help examine the fallen leaves.
4. Finish the scene to record the observation. The leaves stay with the birdwatcher; you do not need a new Bag item.

The scene finds intact leaf edges rather than scorch marks. A warm gust and a bright bird's passage are recorded, along with a smaller visitor copying its cry. This is evidence-gathering, not a wild Moltres encounter.

If the birdwatcher only says he is keeping the leaves for Erika, check both requirements: **win Erika's challenge** and **speak to Oak's aide to file the opening report**. Declining the scene is safe; speak again when ready. Repeated visits confirm an already-recorded observation.

**Optional:** Continue south through Routes 17 and 18 toward Fuchsia for catches or a return visit. This detour is not required for the leaf observation; return east to Celadon when ready to continue to Saffron.

## Sabrina and the teleport pads
Return through **Celadon → Route 7 → Saffron**. Sabrina's Gym is in the **northeast of Saffron**. Heal, save, speak to the entrance guide and choose Standard or Champion.

Ask the Gym staff for directions if the pads are confusing. Their route to the centre is: **take the entry pad, then top left, then bottom left, then bottom left once more**. Retrace those pads to return. Follow the room layout carefully rather than stepping onto every pad at random.

Reach **Sabrina**, agree to the battle, win and finish her dialogue. Dark, Ghost and Bug coverage can help against Psychic opponents; consider coverage moves and secondary types before committing a partner. Your party is not rescaled for either difficulty.

Sabrina's clue points to a researcher on Route 8 who heard two different calls from one hiding place. Her victory records the Gym task, but you still need to visit the researcher to record the field task.

## Route 8 call observation
1. Leave Saffron through its **east gate onto Route 8**.
2. Find the **researcher beside the grass** and speak to them.
3. Agree to stand quietly and listen.
4. Finish both cries and the following dialogue to record the observation.

You hear two different calls from the same hiding place. The scene deliberately leaves their source unidentified; hearing a cry is not proof that the corresponding Pokémon can be caught from that bush. Use the standard encounter list below for actual route catches.

If the scene is unavailable, confirm that you **won Sabrina's challenge** and **filed the opening report** at the Fan Club. Declining lets you return later. Once recorded, the researcher reminds you to bring the observation to Oak's aide.

## File The Borrowed Voice report
Return to **Vermilion's Fan Club**, using Route 8 west to Saffron and Route 6 south to Vermilion. Speak with **Oak's field aide**.

The aide lists each missing task. Complete any missing Erika/Sabrina record or corresponding observation, then return. When all four tasks are complete, the aide files the **field report once** and confirms the distinction between a bright migrating bird and a separate, smaller imitator. **Mew remains a theory**, not a confirmed encounter or reward.

You have now completed **all four currently playable visiting Gyms** and the first two survey stages. Your Trainer Card's Kanto strip shows those victories. You can revisit witnesses and the aide to review the evidence without repeating the Gym battles.

## Continue to The Quiet Current
The field report unlocks survey interactions at the **Power Plant**. Continue to [[walkthrough-kanto-current|Chapter 18: The Quiet Current]] for the route through Rock Tunnel, electrical-feed tasks and an optional Zapdos encounter. Capturing a legendary is not required to advance the survey.

The remaining four visiting Gyms and Articuno/Moltres/Mew expeditions are still future content. You can also keep exploring or take the ferry home whenever you want.

articles.title: First-time item descriptions
articles.summary: How item discovery windows work and what happens on older saves.
articles.content:
## Learn about a new item
For supported gifts, field pickups, hidden items and harvest scripts, the first receipt of an item shows its description in a small top window. The normal receipt dialogue and item icon remain. Advance the receipt normally with A; subsequent receipts keep the icon without repeating the description.

The description explains the item; it does not use it automatically. Inspect your Bag afterward when you want to equip or use it. TM descriptions can also appear at first receipt.

## Existing saves
Item discovery history starts tracking after the upgrade. Older receipts cannot be reconstructed, so an item you owned before upgrading may still show its description the next time you receive it. The history is saved with your game; this feature does not reset your stored Pokémon or inventory.

This covers supported receipt scripts, rather than every way a developer tool or trade can modify the Bag. See [[options|Text Speed]] if you want Instant text; you still confirm dialogue pages yourself.

articles.title: Chapter 18: Rock Tunnel and The Quiet Current
articles.summary: Cross Rock Tunnel, make the Power Plant feeds safe and observe or optionally challenge Zapdos.
articles.content:
## Start the northern survey
First file **The Borrowed Voice** with Oak’s field aide in the **Vermilion Fan Club**. That means Erika and Sabrina’s victories and both Route 16/Route 8 observations must be recorded. The aide now introduces **The Quiet Current** and names any missing Power Plant tasks.

You do not need another Gym badge or an invitation item beyond the Kanto access you already have. Bring healing items, Repels if wanted, and suitable Poké Balls if you plan to challenge Zapdos. **Catching or fighting Zapdos is optional**; observation alone lets you finish the story stage.

## Lavender to Rock Tunnel
From Vermilion, take **Route 6 north to Saffron**, then **Route 8 east to Lavender**. From Lavender, follow the newly open road **north onto southern Route 10**, then enter **Rock Tunnel**.

Use **FIELD → Flash** to improve visibility; no party member needs the move in a moveslot. Follow the connected passages and ladders between **1F and B1F** toward the northern exit. A cave guide reminds you that the exit leads to a Pokémon Center and river. Keep your team healthy as you cross, or use Repels to reduce extra battles.

The route and both tunnel floors have their native FireRed wild levels. These are ordinary catches, independent of the much stronger visiting Gym teams. Check the encounter panels below for each floor’s Pokémon and methods.

## Route 10 and the river
Leave the tunnel onto **northern Route 10** and heal at its **Pokémon Center**. Save before the river journey.

Follow the bank **east from the Center**, use **Surf**, and travel **downriver toward the Power Plant**. Land by the building and enter through its main door. The road toward **Route 9 and Cerulean is still closed**; it is not the path for this survey.

The return can use the main door. A small west path also leads back from the roost’s side exit. Keep the full-region map as an orientation aid, rather than assuming every road drawn on it is open.

## Make both unused feeds safe
Speak with the **technician inside the Power Plant**. You are isolating unused feeds, not turning the plant back on. Inspect the two terminals in either order:

1. **West feed:** the terminal on the **left wall of the first room north of the entrance**. Agree to isolate it and finish the meter-reading dialogue.
2. **East feed:** the **center terminal on the long southern wall**, beyond the entrance corridor. Agree to isolate it and finish the observation of the small prints and copied call.

Each finished task is recorded once. Returning to a completed terminal confirms it is safe. If you decline, you may inspect it again later. If either terminal asks you to file The Borrowed Voice, return to Oak’s aide at the Fan Club; Gym victories and field scenes alone do not substitute for filing that report.

Do not approach the roost expecting the observation to start until **both feeds** are isolated. The aide can identify the missing feed if you lose track.

## Observe Zapdos at the roost
Follow the winding halls to the **northwest roost** and speak to the bird once both feeds are safe. Finish its cry and observation dialogue to record **Zapdos**. The evidence links the local meter readings to the bird’s charge, rather than another Hoenn weather crisis.

When asked whether to challenge it at **level 50**, choose **No** if you want to leave it undisturbed. Your observation remains complete and you can return directly to Oak’s aide. Gym Standard/Champion choices do not change Zapdos’s level.

## Optional Zapdos battle
If you choose **Yes**, you enter a scripted legendary battle with level 50 Zapdos. Save and prepare before agreeing. Bring Poké Balls, avoid overly strong attacks that could knock it out, and use a suitable status move if your team has one. As Electric/Flying, it normally avoids Ground attacks and Electric paralysis; choose your catching tools accordingly.

- **Caught:** the capture persists and the bird is removed from its roost.
- **Fainted or fled:** it returns on a later visit, allowing another attempt. Your survey observation stays recorded.
- **Declined:** it remains undisturbed; you may revisit to choose a battle later.

This is not a random Power Plant encounter slot, so it is described here separately from the standard walking table. You do not need to catch it before filing the report.

## Return and file The Quiet Current
Leave the Power Plant, return along Route 10 and Rock Tunnel to Lavender, then **Route 8 → Saffron → Route 6 → Vermilion**. Speak to **Oak’s field aide in the Fan Club**.

The aide needs the **west feed, east feed and Zapdos observation**. Missing tasks are listed. Once all three are recorded, the aide files **The Quiet Current report** and discusses the smaller prints and copied call separately from Zapdos. Mew remains a theory.

The Adventure Log records survey milestones. For an actionable missing-task checklist, speak to the aide rather than relying only on the log’s history.

## The current endpoint
The next lead is **Seafoam’s cold water**, with Koga helping plan that survey. In **v0.0.40**, the island expedition and new Articuno, Moltres and Mew encounters are not open. The remaining four visiting Gyms are also still in development.

You have reached the implemented story endpoint after filing this report. Explore accessible routes, revisit optional activities, try Zapdos later if you declined or missed the capture, or take the ferry home. There is no extra Seafoam trigger to search for in this release.
